summary.headline: Trustees provisionally approved $6,775 from State Aid for additional security cameras pending legal review of liability terms.
summary.summary: The Library Board of Trustees voted 4-1 to provisionally approve a $6,775 quote from Custom Alarm to install additional security cameras downstairs, funded through the State Aid account pending legal review of vendor liability clauses. Trustees also discussed preparations for the upcoming Annual Town Meeting, Candidates Night logistics following a rejected catering donation from Wegmans, and the annual performance evaluation process for the library director. Facilities Director John Parent joined the meeting to address camera maintenance and building upkeep.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The trustees approved meeting minutes from January 24 and February 9, 2026. The director confirmed that previously overdue minutes from July had been resolved with the Town Clerk.
key_details: Minutes from January 24 and February 9 were accepted unanimously.
A clerk's office filing discrepancy regarding July minutes was confirmed resolved.

topics.title: Director's report on budget, parking, and IT
topics.summary: The director provided updates on staff payroll, snow removal issues impacting handicap parking, and computer replacement plans. Projections show the library is tracking close to its personnel budget, with little to no turnback expected at fiscal year-end.
key_details: Full-year staffing projections showed the library might turn back as little as $76 to the town.
Recent snowstorms left handicap parking stalls across from the entrance iced over and unusable, prompting temporary permission for patrons to park by the book drop.
The library is working with CW MARS and town IT to schedule replacements for aging catalog terminals.
topics.outcome: Discussion only; no formal vote taken.

topics.title: Candidates Night and programming discussion
topics.summary: Trustees reviewed plans for the annual Candidates Night tentatively scheduled for April 29, 2026. The board also discussed catering sponsors, fundraising ideas for the Friends of the Library, and non-resident attendance at children's programs.
key_details: Candidates Night is tentatively scheduled for Wednesday, April 29, 2026, with the Select Board race being the primary contested election.
Wegmans declined to donate catering funding after contributing in previous years, leading the board to consider Roche Bros., Stop & Shop, or trustee baking.
A trustee noted that all attendees at a recent toddler music program were non-residents, prompting discussion on library reciprocity, donation jars, and Friends memberships.
topics.outcome: Trustee Janet Maney agreed to moderate Candidates Night; director will explore catering options.

topics.title: FY27 operating budget update
topics.summary: The director reported that the revised FY27 library operating budget was submitted for the Town Meeting warrant. The finance director acknowledged the library's budget reductions without further change requests.
key_details: The reduced library budget voted at the prior meeting was incorporated into the draft Town Meeting warrant.
The Select Board and Advisory Committee were scheduled to hold a final warrant review that evening.
topics.outcome: No action needed; budget proceeds to Town Meeting.

topics.title: Security camera quote and liability review
topics.summary: The board considered a $6,775 quote from Custom Alarm under the MHEC contract to install three to four additional security cameras in the library basement, Eaton Room, and children's room emergency exit. A trustee strongly objected to standard contract clauses limiting vendor liability to $250 and requiring town indemnification for vendor negligence.
key_details: The project cost is $6,775 for hardware, hard drive storage, and installation.
The quote is being funded from the State Aid account, which has an available balance of $148,625.03.
Facilities Director John Parent joined to confirm Custom Alarm is used town-wide and provides one-year warranty coverage and ongoing facility repairs.
Town Counsel is conducting a legal review of the vendor's liability and indemnification terms.
topics.outcome: Motion passed 4-1 to provisionally approve the contract and authorize funding from State Aid pending town counsel review.
topics.why_it_matters: Authorizes $6,775 in town-held State Aid funds to expand camera surveillance in public library spaces while navigating legal liability risks.

topics.title: Library staff appreciation week
topics.summary: Trustees coordinated logistics and meal schedules for Library Staff Appreciation Week, planned for the second week of April.
key_details: Events are planned for Tuesday through Friday during the week of April 12-17.
Trustees volunteered to provide breakfast and lunches on designated days.
topics.outcome: Schedule to be finalized via email coordination.

topics.title: Library emergency disaster plan
topics.summary: The director provided an update on drafting a comprehensive emergency and disaster response plan for the library following recommendations from the Police Department.
key_details: The plan builds on recommendations from police active-shooter training conducted earlier in the year.
Draft incorporates procedures for staff service points, electronic card door access, and facility emergencies.
The finalized plan will be distributed to staff, the police chief, the fire chief, and facilities director.
topics.outcome: The director will complete revisions following Town Meeting.

topics.title: Library director annual evaluation process
topics.summary: The board discussed the process and format for the director's annual performance review, his first under a full-year contract. Trustees agreed to use the town's Salary Administration Plan appraisal categories as a conversational framework.
key_details: The director will submit his annual self-evaluation document prior to the April meeting.
Evaluation criteria include leadership, communication, job knowledge, productivity, and interpersonal skills.
Trustee reviews will be compiled into a unified performance appraisal.
topics.outcome: Self-evaluation to be circulated before the April meeting.

topics.title: Annual Town Meeting presentation and materials
topics.summary: Trustees discussed the library's presentation and informational flyer for the Annual Town Meeting on April 11, 2026. The materials will feature museum pass cost savings, programming statistics, and the digital collection.
key_details: Town Meeting is scheduled for Saturday, April 11, 2026.
The presentation will include the Peggy Tuttle Award and a brief overview of library operations.
A two-sided handout will highlight Hoopla digital streaming usage and Friends of the Library contributions.
Trustee Jane Davis volunteered to assist the director in preparing the handout.
topics.outcome: Draft handout to be shared with trustees for feedback.

votes.motion: To provisionally approve the contract with Custom Alarm for library security cameras funded from the State Aid account, pending feedback from Town Counsel regarding liability language, leaving judgment to the library director.

upcoming.what: Next Library Board of Trustees regular meeting
